# A query is a box the store holds, found by the declaration it belongs to and
# the arguments it was asked with — so a *call* is what becomes the lookup, not
# the declaration. sngl:remote/http's `fetch` is the case that forced it:
# rewriting the declaration's body worked only for a query the program wrote
# beside its own code, because nothing emits an imported package's functions.
# The call was left standing against a name the output did not contain.

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea --out out app.sngl

# The lookup, keyed by what this call site passed.
grep 'remote\.Query\[Result\]' out/model.go
grep '\[\]any\{m\.url\}' out/model.go
grep '"fetch"' out/model.go

# And inside the thunk, the transport the language implements — the query body,
# through the override, down to the Go package that performs the request.
grep 'http\.Get\(m\.url\)' out/model.go

# Nothing calls the query by name: it has no existence as a function here.
! grep 'm\.fetch\(' out/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"
import http "sngl:remote/http"

component main {
    var url = "https://example.com/"
    var res = http.fetch(url)

    window(title="fetch") {
        text(value=res.or(blank).body)
    }
}

const blank = http.Result{status=0, body="", headers={}}

output(lang="go", platform="bubbletea")
